findings.finding: The plan asserts that editing criteria_routing.json is safe for outstanding attestations because 'ADR 0053 (ticket 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e) ... GRANDFATHERED at the claim gate — outstanding attestations stay valid and report non-blocking registry_drift — so no re-review of the ~40 open/in_progress attested tickets is required.' findings.finding: The plan renames the Epic heading label in `completion_verifier.md:59` from `## Success Criteria` to `## Acceptance Criteria`, but does not address backward compatibility for existing plan documents (in-flight tickets, archived plans, or any plan templates) that still carry a `## Success Criteria` heading. If the verifier prompt does exact or near-exact heading matching, those existing plans would be silently mis-verified after the change. The plan acknowledges ADR 0053 grandfathering only for registry_drift from `criteria_routing.json`, not for the verifier's ability to locate the heading section in older artifacts.
findings.location: Scope section — `completion_verifier.md:59`; Approach section (ADR 0053 / grandfathering discussion)
scenarios: An in-flight plan with `## Success Criteria` is run through the updated completion_verifier; the verifier fails to locate the section and either errors or silently skips AC verification.
A plan template file in the repo still instructs authors to write `## Success Criteria`; new plans built from it fail verification after this change.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC that runs `grep -rniE '^## Success Criteria' docs/ plans/ templates/` (or equivalent path) and either (a) lists the count as zero (clean), or (b) accepts the old heading as an alias in the updated verifier prompt alongside `## Acceptance Criteria` until all documents are migrated.

findings.finding: The plan's scope excludes `det_floor.py:227`, which contains a deterministic decision rule `re.search(r'^##\s+Success Criteria', ...)` that awards epic tickets 2 clarity-score points for the heading this rename removes. After migration, epics will carry `## Acceptance Criteria`, so this branch will silently score 0 for every renamed epic — a degraded DET floor signal with no acknowledgment or compensating fix in the plan.
scenarios: An epic that migrates its heading from `## Success Criteria` to `## Acceptance Criteria` (following the renamed prompt guidance) will receive a clarity_score 2 points lower, potentially pushing it below a gate threshold.
A later sweep auditing 'Success Criteria' usages for this story's goal would not catch this because det_floor.py is excluded from the plan's grep AC, creating a false-clean signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `det_floor.py:227` to the Scope section. Change the regex from `r'^##\s+Success Criteria'` to `r'^##\s+Acceptance Criteria'` (or `r'^##\s+(?:Acceptance|Success) Criteria'` as a transitional fallback). Add an AC: `grep -n 'Success Criteria' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` returns no matches (or the match is the transitional OR-pattern).
